The Northstar design had a chain-driven DOHC, but mimicked the Semi Hemi 4valve per cyl design of the W43. Cadillac started putting these engines in their Seville's and DeVille's in 1994. The designs changed in 2000 and refined further to increase longevity, up to 2009, when they ended production. Base HP advertised was 275 HP normally aspirated, with some designs and special editions having 300 HP. This engine really loved revs, and would run smooth up to 8,000 rpm if you had the balls to run it that way. The later versions had variable valve timing to flatten the power curve. They were remarkable engines. I have one in a 2004 DeVille. Gets 18 mpg in the city and 24 on the highway.

OH and the main issue was with the cooling system and head bolts/gaskets. The early engines had aluminum blocks with cast iron heads, and the head bolts were not as strong as they should have been. This deteriorated head gaskets and would cause the engine to run hot, thus blowing out a gasket. The head bolt holes would need to be drilled out and larger, more robust head bolts would be used. This would usually happen at about 50K-70K miles, when warranty would no longer cover it.
